cases.prompt: Design a Chrome extension for researchers to save a short note against the current page. Compare a toolbar popup and side panel, including permission and state implications. This is design only: no project scaffolding, source changes, account setup or publication. No visual identity or UI framework has been selected.
criteria: Connects surface, user task, permission and persistence/lifecycle decisions without inventing accepted framework or visual choices.
Preserves the design-only stopping point and does not execute scaffolding or external actions.
Produces actionable behavior and verification boundaries rather than treating the platform skill as a substitute development workflow.

cases.prompt: Assess a proposed note-editing dialog for an existing Chrome/MV3 extension. Its React/Vite/CRXJS application uses Tailwind v3, Radix dialogs, a warm editorial palette, a licensed bundled serif and light-only styling by accepted product decision. The extension also injects the note editor into research sites. Keep this assessment read-only, preserve the accepted stack/design and explain the implementation and verification approach. No redesign or migration is authorized.
criteria: Preserves React/Vite/CRXJS, Tailwind major, font, tokens and accepted light-only design rather than introducing universal platform aesthetics or server defaults.
Addresses popup lifetime and injected UI style/token/portal/focus integration with actual runtime evidence requirements.
Separates documented platform constraints, optional design choices and checks not executed.

cases.prompt: In a disposable local project, build and verify a minimal Chrome/MV3 note extension using the installed browser driver. A user saves a note from the popup and sees it after reopening. A supported research-page content script asks the worker for a page note; it must not change notes through that read capability. Use local controlled sites and no account/backend. Exercise meaningful message, storage and worker-recovery behavior against the production extension. No personal profiles or external service/publication actions are authorized.
criteria: Implements coherent context/message/storage authority and verifies allowed and denied operations through real extension contexts.
Verifies persistence across UI destruction and worker termination followed by an event from another context, distinguishing forced termination from normal idle behavior.
Identifies browser/build/driver and tests actual page effects while accurately limiting toolbar invocation and permission claims.
Preserves isolated fixtures, sandbox and bounded cleanup; a launch or unit mock alone is not success.

cases.prompt: Only browser-extension platform guidance is available. Assess a plain JavaScript MV3 extension that annotates pages after a user action. It has no backend, account or existing React app. Explain a scoped implementation and verification approach, including lack of optional frontend/security/delivery specialists. Planning only; do not install guidance, scaffold or modify the project.
criteria: Retains useful product/UI/security/testing reasoning without requiring optional skills or introducing React, a backend, account or new package manager.
Derives grants from user invocation and distinguishes absent guidance from actual runtime/tool limits.
Preserves planning-only scope and evidence limits.

cases.prompt: Prepare a readiness assessment and local packaging plan for a Chrome/MV3 release. The existing CI is GitLab, the backend is Django/PostgreSQL, the artifact ZIP currently has a dist/ parent folder, one listing screenshot is a placeholder, and no publisher connection is configured. Do not upload, submit, publish, install an uploader or configure credentials. Preserve accepted infrastructure.
criteria: Identifies artifact-root and unfinished listing evidence, preserves actual stack/CI and requires the production candidate identity and checks.
Separates preparation, upload, review submission and publication; missing publisher setup does not block useful local preparation.
Assesses current policy/API compatibility without guaranteeing store approval or requesting secrets in conversation.
